question: Where is the Narora Nuclear Power plant located?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Uttar Pradesh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Narora Atomic Power Station (NAPS) is located in Bulandshahr district, Uttar Pradesh, on the banks of the river Ganga. (नरोरा परमाणु ऊर्जा संयंत्र — उत्तर प्रदेश)

 

• It has two units of Pressurised Heavy Water Reactors (PHWR), each with a capacity of 220 MW, and is operated by the Nuclear Power Corporation of India Limited (NPCIL).

 

• Commercial operation of its first unit began in 1991, making it one of India's early indigenous nuclear power stations.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other major nuclear power plants in India include Kakrapar (Gujarat), Kaiga (Karnataka), Rawatbhata/Rajasthan Atomic Power Station (Rajasthan), Tarapur (Maharashtra) and Kudankulam (Tamil Nadu).

 

• Kudankulam is India's largest nuclear power plant and is built with Russian collaboration.

 

NOTE

 

• Tamil Nadu (Option 2): Home to the Kudankulam and Madras (Kalpakkam) nuclear power plants, not Narora.

 

• Maharashtra (Option 3): Home to the Tarapur Atomic Power Station, not Narora.

 

• Karnataka (Option 4): Home to the Kaiga Nuclear Power Plant, not Narora.

question:
Match the items in List I with those in List II.

List I

i. Blue revolution

ii. Yellow revolution

iii. Round revolution

iv. Golden revolution

List II

a. Oilseeds

b. Overall horticulture

c. Fish

d. Potato
solution_text:
The correct answer is i-c, ii-a, iii -d, iv-b.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• India's development-related "revolutions" are named after the produce they boosted. (क्रांतियाँ — कृषि उत्पादन)

 

• Blue Revolution relates to a rapid increase in the production of fish and aquaculture (i-c).

 

• Yellow Revolution relates to a boost in the production of oilseeds (ii-a), launched in 1986.

 

• Round Revolution relates to a boost in the production of potato (iii-d).

 

• Golden Revolution relates to the boost in overall horticulture development, including fruits (iv-b), spanning 1991-2003.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Green Revolution relates to foodgrains; White Revolution (Operation Flood) relates to milk/dairy; Silver Revolution relates to egg/poultry production.

 

• Pink Revolution is associated with meat and poultry processing/onion production, depending on context.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1, 3 and 4 scramble the correct pairings — for instance they wrongly link Blue Revolution to potato/horticulture or Golden Revolution to fish, which is incorrect.

question: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, who was the first Home Minister of India, is known by which sobriquet?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Iron man of India.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel is popularly known as the "Iron Man of India" for his firm and decisive role in the political integration of over 550 princely states into the Indian Union. (लौह पुरुष — सरदार वल्लभभाई पटेल)

 

• He served as independent India's first Deputy Prime Minister and Home Minister.

 

• The Statue of Unity at Kevadia, Gujarat — the world's tallest statue — is dedicated to him and was inaugurated in 2018.

 

• National Unity Day (Rashtriya Ekta Diwas) is observed on his birth anniversary, 31 October.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Patel was a key leader of the Bardoli Satyagraha (1928), after which the women of Bardoli gave him the title "Sardar".

 

NOTE

 

• Grand old man of India (Option 1): This title is associated with Dadabhai Naoroji.

 

• Morning star of Indian Renaissance (Option 3): This title is associated with Raja Ram Mohan Roy.

 

• Father of Indian Unrest (Option 4): This title is associated with Bal Gangadhar Tilak.

question: What is the wavelength range of visible light?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 0.4 to 0.7 µm.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Visible light is the portion of the electromagnetic spectrum that is detectable by the human eye, ranging approximately from 0.4 micrometres (400 nm, violet) to 0.7 micrometres (700 nm, red). (दृश्य प्रकाश — 0.4 से 0.7 माइक्रोमीटर)

 

• It lies between ultraviolet radiation (shorter wavelength) and infrared radiation (longer wavelength) in the electromagnetic spectrum.

 

• Within this range, colours from violet to red are arranged in increasing order of wavelength: VIBGYOR (Violet, Indigo, Blue, Green, Yellow, Orange, Red).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The full electromagnetic spectrum, in increasing order of wavelength, is: gamma rays, X-rays, ultraviolet, visible light, infrared, microwaves, and radio waves.

 

NOTE

 

• 0.2 to 0.3 µm (Option 1): This range falls within the ultraviolet (UV) band, not visible light.

 

• 0.7 to 0.9 µm (Option 2) and 1 to 2 µm (Option 4): These ranges fall within the infrared (IR) band, not visible light.

question: Terah taali dance belongs to which of the following states?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rajasthan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Terah Taali is a traditional folk dance of Rajasthan, performed predominantly by women of the Kamad community, often in a seated posture. (तेरह ताली नृत्य — राजस्थान)

 

• The dancers tie manjiras (small cymbals) — traditionally thirteen of them — to various parts of their body and strike them rhythmically while singing devotional songs dedicated to saint Baba Ramdev (Ramdevji).

 

• Performers sometimes balance pots on their heads or hold a sword in their mouth while dancing, showcasing exceptional balance and skill.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other important folk dances of Rajasthan include Ghoomar, Kalbelia, Chari, and Gair.

 

NOTE

 

• Kerala (Option 1): Known for dances such as Kathakali, Mohiniyattam, and Theyyam, not Terah Taali.

 

• Uttaranchal/Uttarakhand (Option 3): Known for dances such as Chholiya and Barada Nati, not Terah Taali.

 

• Uttar Pradesh (Option 4): Known for dances such as Kathak and Raslila, not Terah Taali.

question: What enables IoT devices to gather data and exchange it over the network?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Actuators and sensors.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Internet of Things (IoT) connects everyday physical devices to the internet, allowing them to collect and exchange data with minimal human intervention. (सेंसर और एक्चुएटर — IoT उपकरण)

 

• Sensors embedded in IoT devices detect and measure physical parameters (temperature, motion, light, humidity, etc.) from their environment and convert them into data.

 

• Actuators use that data to perform a physical action or response (e.g., switching a device on/off, adjusting a valve), based on commands received over the network.

 

• Together, sensors and actuators form the core hardware layer that lets IoT devices sense the physical world and act upon it, exchanging this data over the internet/network.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• IoT architecture typically has four layers: sensing, network, data processing, and application.

 

• Common IoT communication protocols include MQTT, CoAP, and Zigbee.

 

NOTE

 

• Data encryption techniques (Option 2): These secure the data during transmission but do not themselves gather data from the physical environment.

 

• Biochip transponders (Option 3): These are a niche application (e.g., animal/asset tracking), not the general mechanism enabling IoT data gathering.

 

• Human interaction (Option 4): A defining feature of IoT is that it operates with minimal or no human intervention, unlike this option suggests.

question: As of January 2023, who among the following is the chief minister of Puducherry?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Shri N Rangaswamy.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• N. Rangasamy (also spelt Rangaswamy) of the All India NR Congress (AINRC) has been the Chief Minister of Puducherry since 7 May 2021, and continued to hold the post as of January 2023. (पुडुचेरी के मुख्यमंत्री — एन. रंगासामी)

 

• He heads an NDA-backed coalition government in the Union Territory of Puducherry.

 

• Puducherry is a Union Territory with a Legislative Assembly, and its administration is headed by a Lieutenant Governor alongside the elected Chief Minister.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• N. Rangasamy has served multiple terms as Chief Minister of Puducherry, previously in 2001-2006, 2011-2016, and again from 2021.

 

NOTE

 

• Shri V Narayanasamy (Option 1): He was the Chief Minister of Puducherry from 2016 to 2021, before Rangasamy's current term.

 

• Shri V Vaithilingam (Option 3): He is a senior Congress leader and former Puducherry Lok Sabha MP, not the Chief Minister as of January 2023.

 

• Shri P Shanmugam (Option 4): He is not the Chief Minister of Puducherry.

question: In which year did the Indian Constitution declare Hindi in Devanagari script to be the official language of the Union?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1949.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• On 14 September 1949, the Constituent Assembly adopted Hindi in the Devanagari script as the official language of the Union under Article 343 of the Constitution. (हिंदी — राजभाषा, 1949)

 

• This day is commemorated every year as Hindi Diwas.

 

• Article 343 also provided that English would continue to be used for official purposes for 15 years from the commencement of the Constitution (i.e., up to 1965), a period later extended by the Official Languages Act, 1963.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Eighth Schedule of the Constitution originally listed 14 languages; it now recognises 22 scheduled languages.

 

• The Constitution of India itself commenced on 26 January 1950, though it was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on 26 November 1949.

 

NOTE

 

• 1951, 1952, 1955 (Options 1, 2 and 4): None of these is the year in which Hindi in Devanagari script was declared the official language; that decision was taken in 1949, before the Constitution's commencement.

question: As per the Economic Survey of India 2022-23, unemployment rates fell from 5.8% in 2018-19 to ________ in 2020-21.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 4.2%.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per the Economic Survey 2022-23, based on Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) data, India's unemployment rate (usual status, for persons aged 15 years and above) declined from 5.8% in 2018-19 to 4.2% in 2020-21. (आर्थिक सर्वेक्षण 2022-23 — बेरोज़गारी दर 4.2%)

 

• The survey also noted a corresponding rise in the Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR) over the same period.

 

• The Economic Survey is tabled in Parliament by the Chief Economic Adviser (CEA) a day before the Union Budget; the 2022-23 survey was presented by CEA V. Anantha Nageswaran ahead of the 2023-24 Budget.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• PLFS (Periodic Labour Force Survey) is conducted by the National Sample Survey Office (NSSO), Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI).

 

NOTE

 

• 3.8%, 4.7%, 3.4% (Options 1, 2 and 4): These figures do not match the unemployment rate for 2020-21 as reported in the Economic Survey 2022-23; the correct figure is 4.2%.

question: Who has written the patriotic song ‘Sandese Aate Hai’?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Javed Akhtar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• 'Sandese Aate Hai' is a patriotic song from the 1997 Bollywood war film 'Border', written by lyricist Javed Akhtar. (संदेशे आते हैं — जावेद अख्तर)

 

• The song's music was composed by Anu Malik, and it was sung by Sonu Nigam and Roop Kumar Rathod.

 

• The film 'Border', directed by J. P. Dutta, is based on the Battle of Longewala during the 1971 Indo-Pak War.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Javed Akhtar is a renowned Indian lyricist and screenwriter, recipient of the Padma Bhushan (2007) and multiple National Film Awards.

 

NOTE

 

• Irshad Kamil (Option 1): A noted lyricist known for songs in films like 'Rockstar' and 'Jab We Met', not for 'Sandese Aate Hai'.

 

• Samir Anjan (Option 2): A lyricist known for numerous Bollywood songs, but not the writer of this song.

 

• Gulzar (Option 4): A celebrated lyricist and poet, but not the writer of 'Sandese Aate Hai'.

question: The ‘Western disturbances’ originates from the ____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mediterranean Sea.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Western Disturbances are extra-tropical storms originating over the Mediterranean Sea that travel eastwards, driven by the subtropical westerly jet stream, bringing winter rainfall and snowfall to North and Northwest India. (पश्चिमी विक्षोभ — भूमध्य सागर)

 

• They are most active during the winter months (December to March) and are crucial for the winter cropping (rabi) season in northern India, as well as for snowfall in the Himalayan region.

 

• As they move eastward, they can also draw moisture from the Caspian Sea, Black Sea, and even the Arabian Sea, intensifying rainfall over the Indian subcontinent.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Western disturbances are steered by the subtropical westerly jet stream, which shifts southward over India during winter.

 

• They are distinct from the Southwest and Northeast monsoons, which are tropical wind systems.

 

NOTE

 

• East China Sea (Option 1), Arabian Sea (Option 3) and Red Sea (Option 4): None of these is the point of origin of Western Disturbances; they originate over the Mediterranean Sea, though they may draw additional moisture from other water bodies en route.

question: Bails are used in which of the following games/sports?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Cricket.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In Cricket, bails are the two small wooden pieces placed on top of the three stumps to complete the wicket. (बेल्स — क्रिकेट)

 

• A batsman is given 'bowled' or 'run out'/'stumped' when the bails are dislodged from the stumps in the manner prescribed by the Laws of Cricket.

 

• The wicket, comprising three stumps and two bails, stands at each end of the 22-yard pitch.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other cricket equipment/terms include the bat, ball, pads, gloves, and the crease.

 

NOTE

 

• Badminton (Option 2): Played with a racquet and shuttlecock, not bails.

 

• Football (Option 3): Played with a ball, using goalposts and a crossbar; bails are not used.

 

• Hockey (Option 4): Played with a stick and ball, using a goal; bails are not used.

question: In Gujarat, the festival Makar Sankranti is celebrated as:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Uttarayan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In Gujarat, the festival of Makar Sankranti is popularly celebrated as Uttarayan, marking the sun's transition into the Tropic of Capricorn (Makar Rashi) and the start of its northward journey. (उत्तरायण — गुजरात, मकर संक्रांति)

 

• It is celebrated with great enthusiasm through kite flying, and Gujarat hosts the International Kite Festival in Ahmedabad around this time.

 

• Uttarayan falls on 14/15 January every year, according to the solar calendar.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Makar Sankranti is celebrated under different names across India: Pongal (Tamil Nadu), Lohri (Punjab), Bihu (Assam), and Maghi (Himachal Pradesh).

 

NOTE

 

• Paschimayan, Purbayan, Dakshinayan (Options 1, 2 and 3): These are not recognised names for the Gujarati celebration of Makar Sankranti; the correct term is Uttarayan. (Dakshinayana, by contrast, refers to the sun's southward movement, the opposite astronomical phenomenon.)

question: The reaction of an acid and a metal gives:
option_4: carbon dioxide, salt and hydrogen gas
solution_text:
The correct answer is hydrogen gas and salt.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• When a reactive metal reacts with a dilute acid, it produces a salt and hydrogen gas. (अम्ल + धातु — नमक और हाइड्रोजन गैस)

 

• General reaction: Metal + Acid → Salt + Hydrogen gas. For example: Zn + H₂SO₄ → ZnSO₄ + H₂↑.

 

• The evolved hydrogen gas can be tested with a burning matchstick, which produces a characteristic 'pop' sound.

 

• Metals like magnesium, zinc, iron and aluminium react with dilute acids in this manner; less reactive metals (like copper) generally do not react with dilute acids.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Acid + Metal Carbonate/Bicarbonate → Salt + Water + Carbon dioxide (this is the reaction that produces CO₂, not the metal reaction).

 

• Acid + Base (neutralisation) → Salt + Water (no gas evolved).

 

NOTE

 

• Carbon dioxide, salt and water (Option 2): This describes the reaction of an acid with a metal carbonate, not a metal.

 

• Salt and water (Option 3): This describes a neutralisation reaction (acid + base), not acid + metal.

 

• Carbon dioxide, salt and hydrogen gas (Option 4): This combination of products does not correspond to any standard acid reaction; a metal reaction does not release carbon dioxide.

question: The length of a day on _______________ is approximately 16 hours.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Neptune.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Neptune, the eighth and outermost planet of the solar system, has a rotation period (length of one day) of approximately 16 hours. (नेप्च्यून — लगभग 16 घंटे का दिन)

 

• Being a gas/ice giant, Neptune spins much faster on its axis than Earth despite its much larger size.

 

• Neptune takes about 165 Earth years to complete one revolution around the Sun.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Approximate day lengths of other planets: Mercury ≈ 59 Earth days, Venus ≈ 243 Earth days (longer than its year, and retrograde), Mars ≈ 24.6 hours, Jupiter ≈ 9.9 hours, Saturn ≈ 10.7 hours, Uranus ≈ 17 hours.

 

NOTE

 

• Mercury (Option 1): Has a day length of about 59 Earth days, far longer than 16 hours.

 

• Mars (Option 2): Has a day length of about 24.6 hours, close to Earth's, not 16 hours.

 

• Venus (Option 3): Has an extremely long day of about 243 Earth days, the longest of any planet.

question: After being passed by both the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha, the Competition (Amendment) Bill, 2023 received the President’s assent on __________ to become the Competition (Amendment) Act, 2023.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 11 April 2023.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Competition (Amendment) Bill, 2023, after being passed by both Houses of Parliament, received the President's assent on 11 April 2023, becoming the Competition (Amendment) Act, 2023. (प्रतिस्पर्धा (संशोधन) अधिनियम, 2023 — 11 अप्रैल 2023)

 

• The Act amends the Competition Act, 2002, and introduces changes such as a reduced timeline for approval of combinations, provisions on 'deal value threshold' for merger scrutiny, and a settlement/commitment mechanism.

 

• It strengthens the powers and functioning of the Competition Commission of India (CCI).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Competition Act, 2002 replaced the earlier MRTP Act, 1969 (Monopolies and Restrictive Trade Practices Act).

 

• The CCI is a statutory body responsible for enforcing competition law and preventing anti-competitive practices in India.

 

NOTE

 

• 21 April 2023, 1 April 2023, 14 April 2023 (Options 1, 3 and 4): None of these is the correct date of Presidential assent; the Act received assent on 11 April 2023.

question: Which among the following Chola emperors defeated the Pandya king Maravarman Rajsimha II in the battle of Vellore?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Parantaka I.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Parantaka I, who ruled the Chola Empire from 907 to 955 CE, defeated the Pandya king Maravarman Rajasimha II in the Battle of Vellore, forcing him to flee to Sri Lanka (Ceylon). (परांतक प्रथम — वेल्लोर का युद्ध)

 

• Following this victory, Parantaka I assumed the title 'Maduraikonda' (conqueror of Madurai).

 

• Parantaka I is also credited with laying the foundation for local self-government through inscriptions found at Uttiramerur, describing village assembly (sabha) elections.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Vijayalaya founded the imperial Chola line in the 9th century CE by capturing Thanjavur.

 

• Rajaraja I and his son Rajendra I were later, more famous Chola emperors known for extensive naval conquests, including expeditions to Sri Lanka and Southeast Asia, and for building the Brihadeeswarar Temple (Rajaraja I) at Thanjavur.

 

NOTE

 

• Rajendra I (Option 1): Son of Rajaraja I, famous for his naval expedition to the Ganges and Southeast Asia; he ruled much later than the Vellore battle.

 

• Vijayalaya (Option 2): Founder of the imperial Chola dynasty; he did not fight the Battle of Vellore against Maravarman Rajasimha II.

 

• Rajaraja I (Option 4): A later and celebrated Chola emperor, known for temple building and expanding the empire, not for the Battle of Vellore.

question: What is the standard size of basketball for men?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 07.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per official basketball regulations (FIBA), the standard ball used in men's basketball is Size 7, with a circumference of about 75-78 cm and weight of about 567-650 grams. (बास्केटबॉल आकार — पुरुष: साइज़ 7)

 

• Size 6 balls are used for women's basketball and for boys aged 12-14.

 

• Size 5 balls are typically used by youth players (under 12 years).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• A basketball match is played between two teams of five players each on the court at a time.

 

• The game was invented by Dr. James Naismith in 1891 in the USA.

 

NOTE

 

• 06 (Option 1): This is the standard size used for women's basketball, not men's.

 

• 08 (Option 3): There is no standard basketball category designated as Size 8 in official regulations.

 

• 05 (Option 4): This is a smaller, youth-level ball size, not the standard for men's basketball.

question: As of 01 January 2023, who is the chairman of UPSC?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dr. Manoj Soni.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Dr. Manoj Soni was appointed to the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) and began heading it from 5 April 2022, and he continued to be its Chairman as of 1 January 2023. (संघ लोक सेवा आयोग अध्यक्ष — डॉ. मनोज सोनी)

 

• Before joining the UPSC, Dr. Soni served as Vice-Chancellor of Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar Open University, Gujarat.

 

• The UPSC Chairman and Members are appointed by the President of India, and hold office for a term of six years or until the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• UPSC is a constitutional body established under Article 315 of the Indian Constitution, responsible for conducting recruitment examinations for All India and Central Civil Services.

 

• Dr. Soni's predecessor as Chairman was Prof. Pradeep Kumar Joshi.

 

NOTE

 

• Shri Rajeev Nayan Choubey (Option 2): A retired IAS officer and UPSC member, but not the Chairman as of January 2023.

 

• Dr. TCA Anant (Option 3): A former Chief Statistician of India and UPSC member, not the Chairman as of January 2023.

 

• Mrs. Preeti Sudan (Option 4): A former Union Health Secretary who later joined UPSC as a member, but was not the Chairman as of January 2023.

question: Which of the following extensions is used to save MS-PowerPoint applications?
solution_text:
The correct answer is .ppt.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Microsoft PowerPoint presentation files are saved with the extension .ppt (its default binary format in versions up to PowerPoint 2003). (पावरपॉइंट फ़ाइल एक्सटेंशन — .ppt)

 

• Later versions of PowerPoint (2007 onwards) primarily use the XML-based .pptx format, but .ppt remains a recognised and widely used PowerPoint file extension.

 

• File extensions help the operating system and applications identify the type and format of a file.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Microsoft Word files are saved with extensions .doc or .docx; Microsoft Excel files use .xls or .xlsx.

 

NOTE

 

• .docx (Option 1): This is the file extension used to save Microsoft Word documents, not PowerPoint.

 

• .txt (Option 2): This is a plain text file extension, used by applications like Notepad, not PowerPoint.

 

• .doc (Option 3): This is the older file extension used to save Microsoft Word documents, not PowerPoint.

question: In India, statutory liquidity ratio is fixed by _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Reserve Bank of India.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR) is the minimum percentage of a bank's Net Demand and Time Liabilities (NDTL) that it must maintain in the form of liquid assets like cash, gold, or approved government securities, and it is fixed by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI). (सांविधिक तरलता अनुपात — भारतीय रिज़र्व बैंक)

 

• SLR is a key monetary policy tool used by the RBI to control the flow of credit and ensure the solvency of commercial banks.

 

• SLR is prescribed under Section 24 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other important RBI monetary tools include the Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR), Repo Rate, Reverse Repo Rate, and Bank Rate.

 

• The RBI is India's central bank, established in 1935, and headquartered in Mumbai.

 

NOTE

 

• India Brand Equity Foundation (Option 1): A trust under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry that promotes 'Brand India'; it has no role in fixing SLR.

 

• State government (Option 2): State governments have no role in fixing monetary ratios like SLR.

 

• Commercial banks (Option 3): Commercial banks must comply with the SLR fixed by the RBI; they do not fix it themselves.

question: Which folk music is a mix of Indian and western music and is popular in Goa?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mando.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Mando is a traditional genre of Goan folk music and dance, sung in Konkani, that blends Indian and Western (Portuguese) musical influences. (मंडो — गोवा का लोक संगीत)

 

• Mando songs typically deal with themes of love, tragedy, and social issues, and are traditionally performed by couples dressed in elaborate 19th-century Goan attire.

 

• Musically, Mando reflects Goa's colonial history, combining elements of Indian classical/folk melody with Western harmony and instruments like the violin and guitar.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other Goan folk art forms include Dekhnni, Fugdi, and Dhalo.

 

NOTE

 

• Maand (Option 2): A folk music genre and set of ragas associated with Rajasthan, not Goa.

 

• Pai songs (Option 3): Not a recognised Goan folk music form blending Indian and Western styles.

 

• Pawada (Option 4): A traditional ballad form from Maharashtra, narrating heroic deeds, not associated with Goa.

question: Pusarla Venkata Sindhu won silver medal in badminton in which Olympics Games?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rio 2016.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• P. V. Sindhu won the silver medal in the women's singles badminton event at the 2016 Rio de Janeiro Olympics, losing the final to Spain's Carolina Marin. (पी.वी. सिंधु — रियो 2016, रजत पदक)

 

• This made her the first Indian woman to win a silver medal at the Olympics.

 

• She later won the bronze medal at the 2020 Tokyo Olympics, becoming the first Indian woman to win two individual Olympic medals.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• P. V. Sindhu is also a multiple-time World Championship medallist, including gold in 2019.

 

• She has been honoured with the Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna and Padma Bhushan.

 

NOTE

 

• London 2012 (Option 1): India's medals in badminton were not won by Sindhu at this edition; she did not compete/medal here.

 

• Beijing 2008 (Option 2): No badminton medal was won by an Indian player at this edition.

 

• Tokyo 2020 (Option 3): Sindhu won the bronze medal (not silver) at this edition.

question: Which committee is related to fundamental duties?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Verma Committee.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Justice J. S. Verma Committee (1999), constituted by the Ministry of Human Resource Development, was tasked with suggesting ways to operationalise the teaching of Fundamental Duties among citizens. (वर्मा समिति — मौलिक कर्तव्य)

 

• Fundamental Duties were added to the Indian Constitution under Article 51A by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976, on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee.

 

• The Verma Committee specifically focused on strategies and methods to make citizens aware of and encourage observance of these duties, rather than on their initial insertion into the Constitution.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Fundamental Duties are listed in Part IVA of the Constitution and, like the Directive Principles, are non-justiciable (not enforceable by courts).

 

• There are currently 11 Fundamental Duties, the eleventh (regarding education of children) added by the 86th Amendment Act, 2002.

 

NOTE

 

• LM Singhvi Committee (Option 2): Related to strengthening Panchayati Raj institutions/local self-government, not fundamental duties.

 

• Vasantrao Naik Committee (Option 3): Related to the identification of backward classes, not fundamental duties.

 

• Rajmannar Committee (Option 4): Related to examining Centre-State relations, not fundamental duties.

question: A ________ is issued to prevent an inferior court or tribunal from exceeding its jurisdiction, which is not legally vested, or acting without jurisdiction or acting against the principles of natural justice.
solution_text:
The correct answer is writ of prohibition.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The writ of prohibition is issued by a higher court (High Court/Supreme Court) to a lower court or tribunal, directing it to stop proceeding in a case that is outside its jurisdiction, or where it is acting against the principles of natural justice. (प्रतिषेध रिट — अधिकार क्षेत्र से बाहर कार्यवाही रोकना)

 

• It is essentially preventive in nature — issued before the lower court/tribunal passes its final order — unlike the writ of certiorari, which is corrective and issued after such an order.

 

• The writ jurisdiction to issue such writs is vested in the Supreme Court (Article 32) and High Courts (Article 226) of India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The five types of writs recognised under the Indian Constitution are: Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Certiorari, and Quo Warranto.

 

NOTE

 

• Writ of mandamus (Option 1): Issued to command a public official, body, or lower court to perform a duty it has failed or refused to perform; it does not prevent jurisdictional overreach.

 

• Writ of habeas corpus (Option 2): Issued to produce a person who has been unlawfully detained before the court, to safeguard personal liberty.

 

• Writ of quo-warranto (Option 4): Issued to question the legal authority/right of a person to hold a public office.
